process: Aromatics - techniques to reduce energy consumption (Sect. 4.4.4.2)
measure: Distillation column with a dividing wall
cost-unit: % investment cost vs conventional two-column system
note: Typically cuts capital and energy costs by approximately 30 % versus a traditional two-column system; economics: investment 20 % less, energy costs 35 % less, 40 % less space. Example: Ruhr Oel, Muenchsmuenster. reprinted from Yildirim et al. 2011

measure: Energetically coupled distillation (overhead vapour of column 1 heats reboiler of column 2)
note: Steam usage reduced by about 50 %; new plants or major upgrades

process: Hydrogen peroxide - energy recovery in distillation (Sect. 12.4.3.1)
measure: Mechanical vapour recompression on the H2O2 concentration evaporator
note: At low feed concentrations a compressor can reduce the energy needed by up to 90 %; uses more electricity, saves steam; high investment
New high-pressure distillation systems reduced steam consumption by 40 %, to 3.0-4.2 kg steam per litre of 96 vol-% ethanol

measure: Vapour recompression on low-pressure distillation columns
note: Energy costs can be reduced by up to 80 % in low-pressure distillation columns with vapour recompression

process: Styrene - techniques to reduce energy consumption in EB dehydrogenation (Sect. 5.4.4.2.1)
measure: Heat recovery from condensation of EB/SM splitter overhead (azeotropic EB-water vaporisation)
note: Condensation of the splitter overhead vapour produces approximately 500 kcal/kg of styrene, used to boil the EB-water azeotrope feed; new installations; in operation in five countries

measure: Heat recovery from liquid residue incinerators
note: Reported heat energy recovery/savings, data collection; no production basis given
